First, two very different problems

\n\n

The word \"second screen\" gets used for two things that have nothing to do with each other, and search results mix them constantly:

\n\n
\n \n \n \n \n \n \n
What you wantWhat to look for
Use your iPad as an extra monitor for your Mac or PCDuet Display, Luna Display, spacedesk, Sidecar
Put your iPhone or iPad's own content on a monitor, full screenshiftscreen, XeOS
\n
\n\n

Most \"shiftscreen alternative\" lists are full of the first category, which is useless if you're in the second. If you don't have a computer in the equation at all, that's the whole point, you need the second row.

\n\n

What the category is trying to work around

\n\n

iOS has no desktop mode. Plug an iPhone into a monitor and iOS mirrors it: a 19.5:9 picture on a 16:9 panel, with black bars filling the difference, everything scaled for a hand. iPads mirror too, in 4:3, unless they have an M-series chip and Stage Manager.

\n\n

Apps in this category get around it by taking over the external display and drawing something built for that shape instead of copying the phone.

\n\n

What XeOS does differently

\n\n

The distinguishing thing is scope. XeOS isn't a full-screen browser with a bigger window, it's a desktop environment.

\n\n \n\n
    \n
  • Windows. Several at once, move, resize, snap to edges, full screen, minimise. A window switcher and an overview of everything open.
    • \n
  • A dock and an apps drawer, with any website installable as its own app with its own icon.
    • \n
  • A real file manager that mounts iCloud Drive folders, folders from the device, and external USB drives, then opens files in place.
    • \n
  • Built-in apps, PDF viewer with annotation, Office file preview, image viewer, media player, Photos with a full-screen slideshow, notes, text editor, calculator, camera.
    • \n
  • A desktop browser, tabs, bookmarks bar, downloads with progress, an encrypted password manager, reader mode, reading list, per-site zoom, find on page.
    • \n
  • A built-in ad blocker, on by default, from EasyList and uBlock lists, compiled into the engine, including YouTube video ads.
    • \n
  • Import from Safari, Chrome, Firefox and Edge for bookmarks and passwords, so signing in isn't a chore.
    • \n
  • Mouse and keyboard support, with the device's own screen as a trackpad when you don't have them.
    • \n
  • Session restore, every window comes back where you left it.
    • \n
\n\n \n\n

The full-screen part, specifically

\n\n

Every window has a green button that removes all interface, title bar, tabs, toolbar, dock, so the content occupies the entire panel. That's what makes video, slideshows and presentations look right rather than boxed in.

\n\n \n\n

What to check before you switch

\n\n

Two honest points, so there are no surprises:

\n\n
    \n
  1. Your other iPhone apps don't run inside it. This is a desktop environment with its own apps plus the web, not iOS on a monitor. For most desk work that's fine; for a specific native app, it isn't.
    2. \n
  2. Some embedded frames resist clicks from the external screen. Every iOS browser must use WebKit, and cross-domain frames, consent banners, some sign-in and payment boxes, are hardened against programmatic input on purpose. XeOS's answer is a button that hands the page to your phone's screen for that one tap and sends it straight back; see the guide.
    3. \n
\n\n

Getting started

\n\n

You need a cable, USB-C to HDMI, or a Lightning Digital AV Adapter on older iPhones, or an AirPlay receiver. A Bluetooth mouse makes an enormous difference and costs very little. The setup guide walks through the whole thing, including picking the right resolution so you get no black bars.

\n\n
\n

XeOS: External Display Browser turns an iPhone or iPad into a full desktop on any monitor, TV or projector.

\n

Download XeOS on the App Store

Frequently asked

\n\n

Is this the same category as Duet Display or Luna Display?

\n

No, those turn an iPad into an extra monitor for a computer. This puts your iPhone or iPad's own content on a monitor, with no computer involved.

\n\n

Does it need a specific iPhone or iPad?

\n

Any device that can output video to a display. No M-series chip, no Stage Manager.

\n\n

Does it work over AirPlay as well as a cable?

\n

Yes, though a cable is lower latency and can charge at the same time.

\n\n

Will my logins carry over?

\n

Import bookmarks and passwords from Safari, Chrome, Firefox or Edge, see the import guide.
